transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, well, I hope I'm in the right place, and I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining or being lazy... but I came in because I’ve just been so tired. Well, all the time, really. 

I know everyone gets tired, and I always try my best to just push through it, but... by midmorning at work—I'm a claims adjuster—after just reviewing a few files or, you know, walking a junior adjuster through a claim, it just feels like my body and my brain are already completely running on empty. 

I feel a little silly even bringing it up, but... is that an okay reason to be here? Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this tired?

Oh, um... well, it's been quite a while, actually. I feel a little embarrassed admitting it because I probably should have come in sooner, but... I'd say it's been going on for about three years. Maybe three years and three months? 

It started right around the time they moved me into a higher-responsibility role at work. They asked me to start mentoring the other adjusters and overseeing the new workflow systems. Which was a wonderful opportunity, really, and I'm so grateful they trusted me with it! I don't want it to sound like I'm complaining about the promotion or that I can't handle it. I just... I guess that's when I really started noticing how drained I was feeling. 

I kept thinking I would eventually just get used to the new pace and bounce back, you know? I hope it's okay that I waited this long to bring it up... is it normal to take that long to adjust to a change like that?
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since you started feeling tired?

Oh, um... well, I really hate to say yes, because I don't want to sound ungrateful. I have a wonderful life, I really do. But... I suppose I have been feeling a bit down. 

It's just... most days, I feel like there's a sort of gray film over everything? I mean, I still do everything I need to do! I go through the motions and make sure everyone is taken care of, and I always try to keep a smile on my face. But even when my husband is being so sweet and kind, or we're all cooking together as a family—which are things I know I should be so happy about—I just... I don't really feel the enjoyment I used to. 

I feel awful even saying that out loud. I know I should just be happy with what I have, and I really try my best not to let them see it so I don't bring anyone else down. Does that make me sound like a terrible person? I just want to be sure I'm not making too big a deal out of nothing...
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? I really try to keep up with everything, I promise I do. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing. But... I used to love painting on the weekends, and my husband and I would go hiking, and I even used to volunteer... and lately, I just... I haven't been doing those things as much. 

I just feel so bad because I'm barely getting through the week, you know? Like, even at work—and I hate admitting this because I really pride myself on doing a good job—but I've started missing some small details during my audits, and it's taking me a little longer to sign off on files. I'm trying so hard to fix it, I really am. I just... I don't want to let anyone down. Is it okay that I'm struggling with this? I'm not just being lazy, am I?
How long have you been feeling down or sad?

Oh, um... I suppose it's really been about the same amount of time as the tiredness? I'm so sorry, I wish I had a more exact date for you. I really don't want to be unhelpful. 

It's just... I think it all kind of started together, right around that three-year mark when work changed. I kept trying so hard to push through it and put on a brave face for everyone, so I didn't really let myself keep track of when exactly the sad feelings started. I just kept telling myself I was fine, so it all sort of blends together. It just kind of... became my normal, if that makes sense? 

I hope that's an okay answer... I know you probably need specifics for your notes. Am I giving you the right information? I can try to think harder about it if you need me to.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy and look forward to?

Oh, well... I really try to find the good in things, I do. I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining about everything. 

But, um... to be completely honest, I can't really think of anything specific right now that I genuinely look forward to. I mean, I still do things! I still cook dinner and I still go to work, and I try to make sure everything runs smoothly for my family. But that feeling of excitement, or... or really enjoying something? I just haven't felt that in a while. 

I'm so sorry, that sounds so depressing, doesn't it? I know I should be more positive. I really am trying. Is it bad that I don't have a better answer for you? I hope I'm not making your job too difficult...
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I haven't. Um... I'm so sorry if I made it sound like things were *that* bad. I know I've been complaining a lot today, and I really don't want you to worry about me in that way. 

I promise I would never do anything to hurt myself. I'm still trying my best for my husband and my family, and I just want to figure out how to feel like myself again. I hope I didn't alarm you... I'm just having a hard time, but I'm definitely not at that point. 

I hope that's a relief to hear? I just really want to get back on track, I'm not giving up.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I think my eating and sleeping have been pretty normal? 

I know some people get really off track with those things when they're stressed, but I try really hard to keep a good routine. I still make sure to eat three meals a day, and I'm in bed at a reasonable hour. I don't want to let things fall apart, you know? 

Sometimes I might wake up a little early, or maybe I don't finish everything on my plate, but nothing drastic. Nothing that would make you worry, I promise. I hope that's helpful? I'm trying to be as accurate as I can for you.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the tiredness and the gray film over everything, without any significant improvement?

Oh, wow... um, let me think. I don't want to exaggerate it, because I know people go through much worse. But, um... I guess it's been a while now. 

Maybe... about three years? Oh, goodness, maybe three years and three months, if I'm being exact. It started right around the time they promoted me at work. They gave me this higher-responsibility role, mentoring the other adjusters and overseeing all the new workflow systems. 

It's a great opportunity, it really is! I should be so grateful for it, and I am. But I think I just... I haven't quite bounced back since then. I've just been pushing through. I hope I don't sound ungrateful for the promotion... I really do try to do a good job for them. Does that make sense, that it would start around a big change like that?
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now feel neutral or unenjoyable to you?

Oh... um. Well, I feel a little embarrassed to admit this, because I really do try to stay active and involved. But... yes, I suppose so. I used to really love painting, and hiking, and I used to volunteer a lot, too. But lately, I've sort of pulled back from all of that. I'm really just trying to get through the week, to be honest. 

And, um... I hate to even mention this part, because I pride myself on my work, but... I've noticed I'm taking a bit longer to sign off on my files lately. And I might have missed a couple of tiny details in my recent audits. It's nothing huge, I promise! I'm still doing my absolute best to keep everything running smoothly, and nobody has complained. I just... I don't want you to think I'm slacking off or anything. I just don't seem to have the energy for my hobbies right now because I'm trying so hard to keep my head above water at the office. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding lazy... I really am trying to push through it.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

Oh, um... well, I don't know if "pleasure" is the right word, exactly. I mean, I don't really have anything that makes me jump for joy right now, if I'm being completely honest. 

But I do still try to do things! I really do. I'll watch a little TV in the evenings, or maybe read a magazine. It passes the time, and it's fine. It's not that I hate doing those things, it's just... I guess I don't feel that spark of excitement about them anymore? 

I hope that's an okay answer. I know I should probably try harder to find a new hobby or something, and I will, I promise. I just... I don't really have anything specific that I'm enjoying right this minute. Is that alright to say? I'm sorry if I'm not giving you very good answers.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy and now find completely unenjoyable?

Oh, um... completely unenjoyable? No, I don't think so. I really don't want to sound like I'm just miserable all the time or complaining about everything. 

I mean, like I said, I've pulled back from painting and hiking, but I don't *hate* them now. I just... I don't really have the energy for them after work. If I pushed myself to go on a hike, I'm sure it would be fine! I just haven't been doing it. I try to stay positive about things, I really do. 

So, no, I wouldn't say anything is completely unenjoyable. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now you don't enjoy at all?

I'm sorry, I know we sort of just touched on that, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm just complaining! But... I guess to be completely honest, if I have to explain it... it's more like most days I just feel like there's this... this gray film over everything. 

I feel terrible even admitting that out loud. Like, even when my husband is being so sweet and kind, or... or when we're cooking with the family, which is something I've always loved doing... I can go through the motions, but I'm just not really feeling the enjoyment I used to. I still do it, of course! I make sure I'm there and participating because I don't want to let them down. 

I just... I hope that makes sense? I really don't want to sound ungrateful for my family, because they're wonderful, and I know I'm lucky. Am I explaining that okay?
Have you had more than two months where you felt this way, with the tiredness and the gray film over everything?

Oh, gosh, yes... definitely more than two months. I feel like I'm making it sound so dramatic, but... it's actually been a lot longer than that. 

I'd say it's been about, um, three years and three months? Give or take. It started right around the time I got promoted at work. They moved me into this higher-responsibility role where I'm mentoring the new adjusters and overseeing all the new workflow systems. Which is a great opportunity! I was really honored they chose me, and I don't want to sound like I can't handle it. 

But... yeah, that's kind of when this whole feeling started settling in. I hope it's okay that it's been going on for so long before I finally came in to talk to someone about it. I just kept thinking I should be able to push through it on my own, you know? Is that a normal timeline for people to feel this way?
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now you don't enjoy at all?

Oh, um... I know you asked me that a little bit ago, and I really hope I'm not being confusing or difficult! I just... I really wouldn't say there's anything I don't enjoy *at all*. 

Like I said about the family dinners or the hiking... I still do them, and I'm glad I do. I don't hate them. It's just that the joy feels a bit... muted, I guess? But I definitely don't find them completely unenjoyable. I really try to find the good in things. I hope that makes sense? I'm trying to be as helpful as I can.
Has this feeling of tiredness and the gray film over everything been continuous for the past two years?

Oh, yes, it has. I'm sorry, I think I mentioned this just a moment ago, and I don't want to sound like I'm repeating myself or making a bigger deal out of it than it is. But yes, it's been continuous. 

Actually, it's been a bit longer than two years... it's been about three years and three months now. Ever since they gave me that new role mentoring the other adjusters and handling the workflow systems. I really hope it's okay that I let it go on for so long without getting help. I just kept thinking I should be able to manage it myself, you know? Am I answering that right?
Has this feeling of tiredness and the gray film over everything lasted for at least two years without any periods of improvement?

Oh, um... I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm making you ask the same question twice! I really don't mean to be frustrating. But... yes, it's been the whole time. 

I haven't really had any breaks from it. It's just been this steady, quiet sort of heaviness since I got that promotion. I mean, I have good days where I can push through a little easier, and I always make sure my work gets done! But that underlying gray feeling... it hasn't really lifted or gone away at all in these past three years. I hope I'm explaining that clearly? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Has this feeling of tiredness and the gray film over everything lasted without any significant improvement for the majority of the days for at least two years?

Oh, gosh, I am so sorry... I feel terrible that we keep going over this, I must be doing a really poor job of explaining myself! I really don't want to waste your time. 

But, um, yes... it's been the majority of the days. Really, almost every day. I mean, I still get up and do my job and everything, I'm very responsible that way! But that feeling... it hasn't really improved or gone away for more than a day or two here and there since it all started. I'm really sorry if I'm not giving you the answers you need, I promise I'm trying my best to be accurate. Is that what you were asking?
Has this feeling of tiredness and the gray film over everything lasted without any significant improvement for the past two years or more?

Oh dear... I am just... I'm so sorry, Doctor. I feel like I must be doing a terrible job of answering you since we keep coming back to this, and I really, really don't want to be difficult. I promise I'm trying to give you exactly what you need to know! 

But, um, yes... it has definitely been more than two years. It's been about three years and three months now, going all the way back to when they moved me into that higher-responsibility role—you know, the one where I started mentoring the other adjusters and overseeing the new workflow systems? I really hope I'm finally saying this right for you. Does that... does that answer the question properly this time? I can try to explain it differently if I'm still messing it up.
